questions.title: What is the SmartTable, and which annotations drive it (LineItem, PresentationVariant, DataField, restrictions, SemanticObject, Criticality, TextArrangement)?
questions.description: sap.ui.comp.smarttable.SmartTable is a smart control for OData V2 services: you give it an entitySet, and it builds a complete table (columns, toolbar, count, personalization, export) from the service metadata and annotations, instead of you defining every column. The annotations decide what it shows. UI.LineItem is the list of columns: each entry is usually a UI.DataField with a Value (the property path) and optionally a Label and a Criticality; other record types add buttons (DataFieldForAction) or navigation links. UI.PresentationVariant defines the default presentation, such as the initial SortOrder, GroupBy, and which properties must always be requested (RequestAtLeast). Capabilities.SortRestrictions and Capabilities.FilterRestrictions (or the V2 attributes sap:sortable and sap:filterable) tell which columns may be sorted or filtered, so the table does not offer what the service cannot do. Common.SemanticObject on a property turns its values into SmartLinks for navigation to related apps. Criticality (a value or a path in the DataField) colors a value as positive, critical or negative. UI.TextArrangement, together with Common.Text, decides how a code and its description are combined, like "Open (O)" with TextFirst, "O (Open)" with TextLast, TextOnly, or TextSeparate.
keyPoints: SmartTable builds a full table from an entitySet's metadata and annotations (OData V2).
UI.LineItem = the columns (DataField with Value, Label, Criticality; DataFieldForAction for buttons).
UI.PresentationVariant: default sorting, grouping, RequestAtLeast; Sort/FilterRestrictions limit what is offered.
Common.SemanticObject: navigation links; Criticality: colors; TextArrangement + Common.Text: code and text display.

examples.title: Annotations for a SmartTable (CDS syntax)
The SmartTable in a view
examples.code:
<smartTable:SmartTable
  id="ordersTable"
  entitySet="SalesOrders"
  tableType="ResponsiveTable"
  header="Sales orders"
  showRowCount="true"
  enableAutoBinding="true"
  smartFilterId="filterBar" />

questions.title: How do you customize a SmartTable: custom columns, personalization, variant management, the SmartFilterBar link, and the beforeRebindTable event?
questions.description: Several features make the SmartTable flexible. Custom columns: when a column needs a control the annotations cannot describe (like a progress bar or a special button), you put your own inner table (for example a sap.m.Table) into the SmartTable in XML, with your columns, and give each one custom data p13nData with a columnKey and the leadingProperty it is based on; the SmartTable merges these with the annotation-based columns and includes them in personalization. Personalization: with useTablePersonalisation (true by default), the user can choose and reorder columns, and sort, filter and group the data through the settings dialog. Variant management: with useVariantManagement and a persistencyKey, users can save these settings as named views (variants), mark one as default, and share them. SmartFilterBar link: smartFilterId points to a SmartFilterBar, so the table automatically uses its filter values and searches when the user presses Go. The beforeRebindTable event fires each time the table is about to (re)bind its data; its bindingParams parameter lets the controller add filters, sorters, or binding parameters (like expand or select) that are not visible in the UI, for example a fixed filter for the current user. The initialise event fires once the table has been created.
keyPoints: Custom columns: your own inner table/columns with p13nData custom data (columnKey, leadingProperty).
Personalization: choose columns, sort, filter, group (useTablePersonalisation).
Variant management: useVariantManagement + persistencyKey to save named views.
smartFilterId links a SmartFilterBar; beforeRebindTable lets the controller add filters, sorters, or parameters.

questions.title: What is the SmartFilterBar, and which annotations drive it (FilterRestrictions, FieldGroup, ValueList, Hidden)?
questions.description: sap.ui.comp.smartfilterbar.SmartFilterBar builds a filter bar for an OData V2 entitySet from metadata and annotations: it decides which filter fields exist, how each field behaves, and which value helps it offers. Capabilities.FilterRestrictions (or the V2 attributes sap:filterable, sap:required-in-filter and sap:filter-restriction) control filtering: NonFilterableProperties are not offered at all, RequiredProperties must be filled before searching (the field becomes mandatory), and FilterExpressionRestrictions limit a field to a single value, multiple single values, or a single interval (range). UI.SelectionFields lists the fields that are shown in the filter bar by default. UI.FieldGroup groups fields, and the groups appear as sections in the Adapt Filters dialog (the SmartFilterBar's groupConfiguration can also be used). Common.ValueList defines the value help of a field: which entity set provides the values (CollectionPath), which properties are shown in the help dialog, and which are copied back (In/Out parameters); with Common.ValueListWithFixedValues, the field becomes a dropdown instead of a dialog. UI.Hidden hides a property from the UI, so it does not appear as a filter field.
keyPoints: SmartFilterBar builds filter fields for an entitySet from metadata and annotations.
FilterRestrictions: non-filterable, required, and single value / multi value / interval restrictions.
UI.SelectionFields: default visible fields; UI.FieldGroup: groups in the Adapt Filters dialog.
Common.ValueList: value help (fixed values = dropdown); UI.Hidden: the field is not offered.

questions.title: Which SmartFilterBar features should you know: custom filter items, Adapt Filters, variant management, and basic search?
questions.description: Beyond the annotation-based fields, the SmartFilterBar has several features. Custom filter items: when a filter needs a control the annotations cannot express, you add a ControlConfiguration to its controlConfiguration aggregation, with a key and your own customControl (for example a Select or a SegmentedButton); you then turn its value into filters yourself, typically in the linked SmartTable's beforeRebindTable event. A ControlConfiguration can also change an annotation field, for example its label, its position (index), or whether it is visible by default (visibleInAdvancedArea). Adapt Filters: the filter bar has an Adapt Filters button that opens a dialog where the user chooses which filter fields are shown, searches among all available fields, and enters values. Variant management: with useVariantManagement and a persistencyKey, users can save their filter values and visible fields as named variants, choose a default, and reuse them later; with considerSelectionVariants, UI.SelectionVariant annotations can provide predefined variants. Basic search: with enableBasicSearch="true", a free-text search field is added, which sends the search custom query option to the service; this works only if the entity set supports it (sap:searchable). The search event fires when the user presses Go, and a linked SmartTable then rebinds automatically.
keyPoints: Custom filter items: ControlConfiguration with a customControl; convert its value into filters yourself.
ControlConfiguration also changes annotation fields (label, index, visibleInAdvancedArea).
Adapt Filters lets users choose and arrange filter fields; variants save filters (useVariantManagement + persistencyKey).
enableBasicSearch adds free-text search (needs sap:searchable); search fires on Go.

examples.title: A custom filter item and basic search
examples.code:
<smartFilterBar:SmartFilterBar
  id="filterBar"
  entitySet="SalesOrders"
  enableBasicSearch="true"
  useVariantManagement="true"
  persistencyKey="ordersFilterVariants">
  <smartFilterBar:controlConfiguration>
    <smartFilterBar:ControlConfiguration key="Status" index="1" visibleInAdvancedArea="true" />
    <smartFilterBar:ControlConfiguration key="priorityFilter" label="Priority" visibleInAdvancedArea="true">
      <smartFilterBar:customControl>
        <Select id="prioritySelect">
          <core:Item key="" text="All" />
          <core:Item key="H" text="High" />
          <core:Item key="L" text="Low" />
        </Select>
      </smartFilterBar:customControl>
    </smartFilterBar:ControlConfiguration>
  </smartFilterBar:controlConfiguration>
</smartFilterBar:SmartFilterBar>

questions.title: What is the SmartField: its annotations, field types, value help, and field control?
questions.description: sap.ui.comp.smartfield.SmartField is a single smart input or display field. You bind its value to an OData property, like value="{Price}", and it chooses and creates the right inner control from the property's metadata. Field types: in edit mode, it becomes an Input for strings and numbers (with the right type and maximum length), a DatePicker or DateTimePicker for dates, a CheckBox for booleans, an Input with a unit field for amounts with a currency or unit (sap:unit or Measures annotations), and a ComboBox or Select for fields with fixed values; in display mode (editable="false"), it shows a Text, a link, or an ObjectStatus. Its annotations: the label comes from sap:label or Common.Label, a description text from Common.Text (with TextArrangement), and validation from the type facets. Value help: if the property has a Common.ValueList annotation, the SmartField automatically adds a value help dialog with search and filters (and type-ahead suggestions); with ValueListWithFixedValues, a dropdown is shown instead. Field control: through sap:field-control or Common.FieldControl, a property's value decides at runtime whether the field is hidden, read-only, optional, or mandatory, and the SmartField applies this automatically. Settings like mandatory, editable, and the configuration aggregation (controlType) can override the defaults.
keyPoints: SmartField picks its inner control from the bound property's metadata.
Edit mode: Input, DatePicker, CheckBox, ComboBox/Select, amount + unit; display mode: Text, link, ObjectStatus.
Value help comes automatically from Common.ValueList (fixed values = dropdown).
Field control (sap:field-control / Common.FieldControl) hides it or makes it read-only, optional, or mandatory at runtime.

examples.title: SmartFields in a view
examples.code:
<VBox>
  <smartField:SmartLabel labelFor="customerField" />
  <smartField:SmartField id="customerField" value="{CustomerID}" />   <!-- value help from Common.ValueList -->
  <smartField:SmartField value="{OrderDate}" />                       <!-- DatePicker -->
  <smartField:SmartField value="{GrossAmount}" />                     <!-- amount + currency -->
  <smartField:SmartField value="{IsUrgent}" />                        <!-- CheckBox -->
</VBox>

questions.title: What is the SmartForm, and how do annotations affect it?
questions.description: sap.ui.comp.smartform.SmartForm is a form container for SmartFields, used for detail and edit screens. It is organized in Groups (sap.ui.comp.smartform.Group, with a label) that contain GroupElements, each holding one or more SmartFields (or other controls). The SmartForm gives you a lot for free: labels for every field from the metadata (sap:label or Common.Label), a responsive layout (with the layout aggregation, for example a ColumnLayout or a GridData-based Layout, so groups are arranged in columns), and edit handling: with editTogglable="true" it shows an Edit button, and switching its editable property switches all SmartFields inside between display and edit mode at once. checkButton adds a check that validates all fields. The annotations act through the SmartFields: field types, value helps (Common.ValueList), texts and text arrangement, units and currencies, mandatory and read-only state through field control, and UI.Hidden for fields that must not be shown. In annotation-driven apps (like SAP Fiori elements object pages), the groups themselves come from UI.FieldGroup annotations, referenced by UI.Facets, so the form content is defined in the back end rather than in the view.
keyPoints: SmartForm = Groups > GroupElements > SmartFields.
Labels, responsive layout, and one Edit toggle (editTogglable / editable) for all fields.
Annotations work through the SmartFields: types, value helps, texts, units, field control, UI.Hidden.
In annotation-driven apps, groups come from UI.FieldGroup (referenced by UI.Facets).

examples.title: A SmartForm
examples.code:
<smartForm:SmartForm
  id="orderForm"
  title="{SalesOrderID}"
  editTogglable="true"
  editable="false">
  <smartForm:layout>
    <smartForm:ColumnLayout columnsM="2" columnsL="2" columnsXL="3" />
  </smartForm:layout>
  <smartForm:Group label="General">
    <smartForm:GroupElement>
      <smartField:SmartField value="{CustomerID}" />
    </smartForm:GroupElement>
    <smartForm:GroupElement>
      <smartField:SmartField value="{OrderDate}" />
    </smartForm:GroupElement>
  </smartForm:Group>
  <smartForm:Group label="Amounts">
    <smartForm:GroupElement>
      <smartField:SmartField value="{GrossAmount}" />
    </smartForm:GroupElement>
  </smartForm:Group>
</smartForm:SmartForm>

questions.title: What is the dynamic field control concept, and what does the UI.Hidden annotation do?
questions.description: Dynamic field control means the back end decides, for each record and at runtime, how a field behaves in the UI, instead of the UI hard-coding it. For example, a discount field may be editable only while an order is in status New, and mandatory for certain customers. In OData V2, a property gets sap:field-control=" DiscountFC", and in the vocabulary-based annotations Common.FieldControl: DiscountFC (a path), pointing to another property that holds a number: 0 means hidden (in newer guidance, Inapplicable), 1 read-only, 3 optional (editable), and 7 mandatory. The service computes this number per entity, and smart controls and SAP Fiori elements apply it automatically, so the field changes its state when the data changes. Common.FieldControl can also be a fixed value, like #ReadOnly or #Mandatory, for static cases. UI.Hidden is a separate annotation that removes a field (or an action) from the UI completely. It can be static (UI.Hidden: true, for technical fields that should never be shown), or dynamic, with a path to a boolean property (UI.Hidden: IsHidden), so the field is hidden for some records only. The difference: field control describes how an existing field behaves (read-only, mandatory...), while UI.Hidden decides whether it appears at all.
keyPoints: Dynamic field control: the back end sets a field's behavior per record at runtime.
sap:field-control / Common.FieldControl points to a property: 0 hidden, 1 read-only, 3 optional, 7 mandatory.
Static values (#ReadOnly, #Mandatory) are also possible.
UI.Hidden removes a field or action from the UI, statically (true) or per record (path to a boolean).

questions.title: What are side effects for smart fields?
questions.description: A side effect describes that changing one value on the screen affects other values that must then be reloaded from the server. For example, changing the quantity of an order item changes its net amount, and the order's total; changing the customer may change the delivery address. Without side effects, the UI would still show the old totals until the page is reloaded. The Common.SideEffects annotation declares this on an entity type: SourceProperties (or SourceEntities) are the triggers, like Quantity, and TargetProperties (or TargetEntities) are what must be refreshed, like NetAmount and the navigation to the order header; optionally, a TriggerAction names a function import that the server should run first (for example to recalculate). Smart controls and SAP Fiori elements (in V2 mostly together with draft handling) read this annotation: when the user changes a source field and leaves it, the framework sends the change and then requests the target properties again, so the dependent values update on the screen right away. Side effects keep the calculation logic in the back end, in one place, instead of duplicating it in the UI.
keyPoints: A side effect: changing a value requires other values to be reloaded (totals, dependent fields).
Common.SideEffects: SourceProperties/SourceEntities trigger, TargetProperties/TargetEntities are refreshed.
Optional TriggerAction: a function import the server runs first.
Smart controls / Fiori elements send the change and reload the targets automatically; the logic stays in the back end.
